from the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua
it is written "an assembly to Hashem your God" (Devarim 16:8),
and it is written "an assembly shall it be for you" (Bamidbar 29:35);
half of it for Hashem and half of it for you,
or all of it for Hashem, etc.,
Now in truth the two pesukim were stated
Regarding the seventh day of Pesach
it says "shall it be for you."
they learned through a gezeirah shavah
to apply what is said of this one to that one.
the mitzvah lies specifically upon the outer garment,
from the pleasures of this world in actual fact,
by eating the bread of affliction.
which is the season of our rejoicing,
that is, upon the outer garment
there should be the aspect of "for you."
And this is the purpose of the derivation
to apply what is said of this one to that one:
meaning that the body too should enjoy
and feel vitality from the kedushah
as it does from the matters of this world;
and on the festival of Shemini Atzeres
the "for you" should also be "for Hashem,"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁגַּם כׇּל הֲנָאוֹת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
meaning that all the pleasures of this world as well
should be solely for Hashem alone.
וְעַל זֶה רָמְזוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה:
that the "for you" should also be "for Hashem";
It is the day on which the Torah was given.
For through the power of the Torah
upon all the creations in this world,
is only to do the will of their Maker,
as it says in the Gemara (Chullin 7a)
"I am going to do the will of my Maker,"
that is, without any free choice on its part.
And just as it was in this aspect
״אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כט),
and the delights of this world
מִכֹּל עֵץ הַגָּן אָכֹל תֹּאכֵל״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, טז).
of every tree of the garden you may surely eat" (Bereishis 2:16).
And with this we will also understand
that it was a fast over a dream,
and therefore even on Shabbos and Yom Tov,
it is permitted to sit in fasting,
regarding which the term "feasting" is used;
eating itself is reckoned as a fast,
"as though he fasted on the ninth," etc.;
the time when the Torah was given,
of the intent of a fast,
that "the diminishing of my fat and blood should be
as though I had offered a korban."
And this is found stated explicitly
regarding the eating of talmidei chachamim:
one who brings a gift to a talmid chacham
is as though he offered bikkurim (Kesubos 105b);
and one who wishes to pour a libation of wine
שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים יַיִן (יוֹמָא עא, א);
״אִישׁ אֱלֹהִים עוֹבֵר עָלֵינוּ תָּמִיד״ (מְלָכִים ב ד, ט),
"a man of God passes by us continually" (Melachim II 4:9),
whoever hosts a talmid chacham in his home
is as though he offered the daily korbanos.
even a fast over a dream is forbidden,
Rav Yosef, on the day of Atzeres,
said, "Prepare for me a choice third-grown calf."
אָמַר: אִי לָאו הַאי יוֹמָא דְּקָגָרַם,
He said, "Were it not for this day that brought it about,
how many a Yosef there are in the marketplace!"
together with the power of his Torah,
as against the rest of the unlearned;
and were it not for Matan Torah,
what would distinguish one man from other men?
"And it would be, as with the people, so with the Kohen" (Yeshayah 24:2).
there were many lofty and exalted souls
of far greater stature than the rest of the people,
such as the beis midrash of Shem and Ever
and the other great men of the generation.
Also, what is the meaning of the expression
עַל פִּי מֵימְרָא אַחֶרֶת דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
according to another statement of Rav Yosef
who said, "Do not teach 'humility' in the Mishnah,
For in truth Rav Yosef had
to the point that it did not enter his mind
that he had any advantage of his own,
רַק מִצַּד שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
but only that he had a root in kedushah
from the aspect of being bound up
with the totality of the souls of Yisrael.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשֵׁם הָרַב הַקָּדוֹשׁ מִבַּארְדִּיטְשׁוֹב,
And as they related in the name of the holy Rav of Berditchev,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
may the memory of the tzaddik be for a blessing in the life of the World to Come,
the berachah "Who has not made me a gentile";
and when they asked him about it,
he answered that upon rising from his bed
he felt great brokenness of heart,
and he had nothing with which
that at any rate his birth
stems from the root of the kedushah of Yisrael;
and he recited with great joy
the berachah "Who has not made me a gentile,"
and with this he restored his soul.
that from the moment of Matan Torah onward
the souls of Yisrael were set apart
from the souls of the nations of the world,
from a special treasury in kedushah.
וְכׇל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אֲחִיזָה בְּתוֹלָדָה
And whoever has a hold by birth
must necessarily be refined for the good
כְּאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה, א):
until all the souls in the Guf have been used up.
And to this Rav Yosef alludes:
"Were it not for this day that brought it about" —
the souls of Yisrael were set apart,
so that their root would be in kedushah by birth —
"how many a Yosef there are in the marketplace";
for it is known that the name Yosef
denotes the aspect of the tzaddik
And although he knew of himself
that he had not blemished the Bris,
וְאִם כֵּן עַל כׇּל פָּנִים הוּא צַדִּיק,
so that at any rate he was a tzaddik,
yet he, in his lowliness in his own eyes,
thought that this came not from his own striving
and his overcoming of the yetzer,
but only from his natural disposition from birth,
and that the yetzer had left him alone in this.
there are found a number such as these,
as is known from the story of the Baal Shem Tov
that all the deeds of the nations of the world
are reckoned as nothing and naught,
except for the souls of Yisrael,
stem from the root of kedushah,
עַל פָּסוּק ״שִׁמְעוּ כִּי נְגִידִים אֲדַבֵּר״ (מִשְׁלֵי ח, ו),
on the pasuk "Hear, for I will speak noble things" (Mishlei 8:6),
that for each and every utterance
that went forth from the mouth of HaKadosh Baruch Hu
they would tie to it two crowns.
The matter of the two crowns
that to each one of Yisrael
and one corresponding to "we will hear."
that all the faculties of the body should be
prepared for the aspect of doing,
for action depends only on the body.
And "we will hear" refers to the faculties of the soul,
that they should be prepared for the aspect of "we will hear,"
which is the matter of hearing and understanding in the heart.
And the matter of the crowns means
that all the faculties of body and soul
should be encompassed in the aspect of "we will do and we will hear,"
from the lowest level up to the root,
which is the aspect of Keser
And it is also in allusion to this
that the Dibros were ten in number,
that is, that they should be fixed in the souls of Yisrael
throughout the entire chain of the middos
so that they should be fixed within them, in the heart,
וּכְמוֹ כֵן כׇּל דִּיבּוּר בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
So too each utterance in its own right
הַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן הִתְכַּלְּלוּת כׇּל הַמִּדּוֹת
that is, also the inclusion of all the middos
in the body and soul of the utterance,
so that it should endure forever
in all the souls of Yisrael for all generations.
And the body of the utterance
is the actual bodies of the letters;
this is the "we will do" aspect of the utterance.
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז רַשִׁ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
in saying that the utterance had tangible substance
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְכׇל הָעָם רוֹאִים״ (שְׁמוֹת כ, טו);
as it says, "And all the people saw" (Shemos 20:15);
as it says in the Zohar Chadash (Yisro)
that they did not hear the Dibros,
kissing their mouths in a whisper;
rather, they saw the forms of the letters
that were engraved in the darkness.
"And all the people saw the sounds."
And this is what Rashi intends
regarding the crown of the utterance
in the aspect of "we will do,"
namely, the seeing of the bodies of the letters.
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז הַפָּסוּק (יְשַׁעְיָה נה, יא):
And to this the pasuk alludes (Yeshayah 55:11):
"So shall My word be that goes forth from My mouth;
it shall not return to Me empty,
כִּי אִם עָשָׂה אֶת אֲשֶׁר חָפַצְתִּי
but it shall accomplish that which I desire
and succeed in that for which I sent it."
מְרַמֵּז עַל בְּחִינַת מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁל הַדִּיבּוּר,
alludes to the aspect of action of the utterance,
namely, the actual bodies of the mitzvos.
"And succeed in that for which I sent it"
refers to the inner intent of the utterance
in the aspect of the soul,
when the aspect of hearing is completed
in the inner depths of the heart.
And one may explain the juxtaposition with the derashah above
on the pasuk "for I will speak noble things":
has the power to put to death and to give life,
so too words of Torah, etc.;
for those who go to its right it is an elixir of life,
for those who go to its left, etc.
שֶׁלְּכׇל דִּיבּוּר קוֹשְׁרִים לוֹ שְׁנֵי כְתָרִים,
that to each utterance they tie two crowns,
so that it will have, in all the souls of Yisrael,
קִיּוּם בִּבְחִינַת גּוּף וְנֶפֶשׁ שֶׁל הַדִּיבּוּר
permanence in the aspect of the body and soul of the utterance
Although in this world it appears
that there are those who go to the left,
לֹא יָשׁוּב הַדָּבָר רֵיקָם לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא,
the word will not return empty in the time to come,
"but it shall accomplish" and so on,
וְזֶה מְרוּמָּז גַּם כֵּן בַּפָּסוּק (יְחֶזְקֵאל לו, כז):
And this is also alluded to in the pasuk (Yechezkel 36:27):
"And I will put My spirit within you" —
that is, the establishment of will in the soul,
which is the aspect of "we will hear";
"and I will cause you to walk in My statutes" —
which is the perfection of the faculties of the body;
so that there will be fixed within us
the aspect of the body and soul of the Dibros,
and of hearing in the heart,
in the full perfection of the middos up to the Keser,

And Rabbi Chaim Vital wrote in his gloss
for what is mentioned, "seventy faces to the Torah,"
but he did not write a reason

that the masters of Kabbalah, etc.,
are from the side of the Tree of Life;
are from the side of the Tree of Good and Evil,
the time of Matan Torah was
from the side of the Tree of Life
״כִּי בְּרוֹב חׇכְמָה רוֹב כָּעַס״ (קֹהֶלֶת א, יח).
"For in much wisdom is much anger" (Koheles 1:18).
is from the side of good and evil,
And from the side of the Tree of Life
are the seventy faces to the Torah,
and this is the inner dimension.
And this is what it says,
And the forty-nine faces of tahor
of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil,
and they are right and left.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה ב, יג):
And this is what is said in the Midrash Rabbah (Bamidbar Rabbah 2:13):
Avraham is compared to the sun,
the sun and moon will be ashamed, etc.,
but the stars will not be ashamed;
their faces will darken in the time to come
That is, in their words of Torah there was
an intermixture of good and evil,
from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil.
וְכֵן אַחַר שֶׁשִּׁיתֵּף הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
And likewise, after HaKadosh Baruch Hu joined
the attribute of mercy to the attribute of judgment,
that the world could not endure,
then it is written "when they were created" (Bereishis 2:4),
was from the side of the Tree of Life,
and there was no dross or intermixture in him.
from the side of the Tree of Life.
And after the dross left them
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סג, ג, רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תּוֹלְדוֹת),
and they too are from the side of the Tree of Life.
that are from the side of the Tree of Life,
when they include the first three as well,
are the seventy faces of the Torah,
And from the side of the Tree of Good and Evil,
like the creation of the world,
"And one who makes use of the crown," etc.,
sitting and tying crowns to the letters, etc.,
"and Akiva ben Yosef is his name,
שֶׁעָתִיד לִדְרוֹשׁ עַל כׇּל קוֹץ וָקוֹץ
who is destined to expound upon each and every tittle
That is, the utterance from Hashem Yisbarach
is from the side of the Tree of Life,
that are tied to each utterance
and they are right and left.
The holy Zohar counts them in detail:
אַרְבָּעִים וָתֵשַׁע פָּנִים טָהוֹר מֵהַאי גִּיסָא
forty-nine faces of tahor on this side
and forty-nine faces on that side;
while the Gemara counts them in general:
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
That is, through Torah she'b'al peh
they will merit to repair the abundant anger
and will merit words of Torah
from the side of the Tree of Life,
the learning of Torah was implanted in their heart,
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their heart
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, ב);
(as Chazal said in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2);
and so we merit the crowns every year,
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת פח, א):
And this is the meaning of what is said in the Gemara (Shabbos 88a):
Who gave a threefold Torah," etc.
rather, he had a meaning and an allusion
Now Rashi explained "a threefold Torah" as
for on the day of Matan Torah
these had not yet been given;
they would have been given only
the five Chumashim of the Torah,
But according to what has been said,
as referring to the utterance of Hashem Yisbarach
and the two crowns that were tied to it,
that is, the Kohen is the aspect of Chesed,
the Levi is the aspect of Gevurah,
the Yisrael is the aspect of Tiferes,
was on the level of Yaakov Avinu,
(תִּיקּוּנִים, תִּיקּוּן יג, תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר כט, א):
Rather, he was there from the inner side," etc.;
from the side of the Tree of Life;
and also the dialectic of the Torah
that is, the forty-nine faces of tahor
and the forty-nine faces of tamei,
so of itself he encompasses everything,
in that the "threefold" encompasses all three;
whereas according to Rashi's explanation, third-born,
it is not similar to all the other "threefold" terms.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פא, א):
as it is written in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 81a):
And Yaakov Avinu is the totality of the Avos,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קסג, ב),
as it is written in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 163b),
for he encompasses the middos of love and fear,
which are likewise right and left.
in the gloss of Rabbi Chaim Vital
on what is said in the holy Zohar
וְכָתַב רַבִּי חַיִּים וִיטַאל זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
that these are Nissan, Iyar and Sivan,
corresponding to Chesed, Gevurah and Tiferes.
"And the Tiferes" — this is Matan Torah —
and it corresponds to the letter Vav,
which is called the letter of truth,
because it encompasses all seven weeks;
just as Atzeres is after Pesach
And regarding Atzeres the Arizal wrote
that it is a term of absorption,
so as to be purified sevenfold
וּפֶסַח נֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And Pesach corresponds to Avraham Avinu,
came only from the attribute of Chesed;
and the Egyptian exile and the redemption
And Iyar is the aspect of Gevurah,
as it says in Sefer Yetzirah (chapter 5):
"He made the letter Vav king over thought," etc.,
and likewise Taurus in the universe."
That is, to overcome the yetzer hara,
for thought is one of the three things
from which no one escapes each day
and this is "in the third month,"
which are the three middos mentioned,
